summary: The Anglican Church in North America's catechism, To Be a Christian, teaches that Holy Scripture is "God's Word written", given by the Holy Spirit through prophets and apostles as the revelation of God and his acts in history, and is therefore the Church's final authority in all matters of faith and practice. The thirty-nine books of the Old Testament and the twenty-seven of the New together form the whole of Holy Scripture. The fourteen books of the Apocrypha may be read as examples of faithful living but "not to establish any doctrine". The questions read do not say who interprets Scripture.
